To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the myogenic response (myogenic tone) in resistance vessels (small mesenteric arteries) is crucial for maintaining vascular resistance and blood pressure.

(1) the myogenic tone (MR) in mouse small mesentery arteries (SMA, diameter 100−150 μm) is maintained by a G protein‐couple receptor (GPCR)‐activated signaling pathway, (2) GPCR activation leads to an increase in cytosolic free Ca2+ via activation of phospholipase C (PLC), and subsequent release of Ca2+ from intracellular stores and influx of Ca2+ via L‐type
MT in small mesenteric resistance vessels is maintained by Gαq/PLC/Cav/Ca2+ signaling, and by Ca2+ sensitizing Rho‐kinases, and that the latter is increased with age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of MR and MT in small mesenteric vessels, and the effect of aging.
the molecular mechanisms involved in the development of MR in small arteries, and the effect of aging on these mechanisms.
the signaling pathways involved in MT development and the age‐dependent increase of MT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MT in SMAs occurs via Gαq/ 11/PLC‐dependent activation of Rho‐ROCK2‐dependent Ca2+ sensitisation.

the myogenic response and the myogenic tone in small mesenteric resistance vessels are maintained by the G protein‐dependent pathway and the ROCK2‐mediation of Ca2+ sensitivity, and that the myogenic tone is increased with age due to increased ROCK2 expression.
MT in SMA is maintained by G protein‐couple receptors via Gαq/PLC/Cav1.2‐dependent Ca2+ influx, and via Rho‐kinases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the myogenic response is a robust and age‐independent mechanism that is maintained by the Gαq/PLC‐mediated signaling and Ca2+ sensitizing Rho‐kinases.

MT is a complex process involving Gαq/ 11‐ and/or Gαq12‐mediated activation of the PLC‐Ca2+‐dependent signaling pathway, and that the age‐dependent increase of MT can be explained by an age‐dependent up‐regulation of ROCK2.
the Gαq/12/13/PLC/Cav/Ca2+ pathway plays a major role in MT development in SMs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MR in SMA is maintained via Gαq/ 11‐PLC‐Ca2+ signaling, and that increased MT in mature mice may be due to increased ROCK2 expression.
ROCK2‐mediation of MT in resistance arteries can be targeted for treatment of vascular diseases.
the Gαq/ 11/PLC/ROCK2 signaling cascade is a key regulator of the MR and MT in small mesenteric vessels, and that this pathway is affected by aging.
